title: A symmetric heap and a fused all-gather plus GEMM
brief: Build a simulated NVSHMEM-style symmetric heap with puts, signals, fence, and quiet. Write an all-gather from puts, a chunked all-gather plus GEMM schedule that never reads an unsignaled chunk, and an alpha-beta model that picks serial, overlapped, or fused. A two-GPU NCCL overlap timing runs only when the machine has two GPUs.
hints: Start with address. PE p's heap begins at HEAP_BASE + p * PE_STRIDE, and an element is ELEM bytes. The same offset on two PEs differs only by PE_STRIDE.
translate keeps the byte offset into the heap and swaps the base. malloc is a bump allocator that returns one offset, valid on every PE.

put and signal only append to pending. Nothing arrives until step, quiet, or wait_until delivers it. quiet delivers one PE's operations. fence delivers nothing: it raises the epoch, and the network holds a later operation back until every earlier-epoch operation to the same PE has arrived.

The data must arrive before the signal that announces it. Put the data, call fence, then signal. Under the signals_first policy, a missing fence lets the signal arrive first, and the consumer reads stale data.
wait_until spins on step. When step returns False and the word still differs, raise SignalNotReady, because no operation is left to change it.
ag_gemm waits on a chunk's signal before it reads the chunk, and logs ('wait', pe, chunk) then ('compute', pe, chunk). A PE's own chunk needs no wait, and tile_order puts it first.
overlap_model is the formulas in the docstring. Check a case by hand: with chunks = 1 and no launch cost, overlapped and serial differ only by the SM share.
The two-GPU check runs only when this machine has two GPUs. A missing two-GPU endpoint does not send it to the single A100.
